summary: CCC-built 1934/35 R-5 design cab in Plumas NF, NHLR-listed 2007, converted to a Recreation.gov rental cabin in 2011.

facts.design: 14'x14' C3 live-in cab with catwalk, Forest Service R-5 (California region) design, on an 11' enclosed timber tower

access.note: Rentable cabin via Recreation.gov; dirt road access, high-clearance vehicle recommended, combination lock code from Beckwourth Ranger District

events.note: NHLR description says constructed in 1934 by the CCC, though the register's own 'Built' field elsewhere lists 1935
Registered as NHLR US 692 on April 23, 2007
Grand opening as a recreational rental on May 26, 2011, at $60/night

evidence.supports: Built 1934 by CCC, design, dimensions, tower height
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1934 by the CCC, Black Mountain Lookout is a classic C3 14’x14’ live-in cab with catwalk of an original Forest Service R-5 design (California Region). It is mounted on an 11’ enclosed timber tower
Black Mt. L.O. Grand opening on the Plumas National Forest is open as a recreational rental effective May 26, 2011. The fee is $60 per night stay.

evidence.supports: Cabin sleeping capacity, amenities, and tent camping space
evidence.quote: The one-room lookout cabin is set on a tower, rising 10 feet above the ground. It is furnished with two single beds with mattresses, but can accommodate up to four people.

evidence.supports: Access by combination lock and dirt road
evidence.quote: Entry to the cabin is by key; contact the Beckwourth Ranger District at (530) 836-2575 for the combination to the lock box

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR's narrative description says 1934 ('Constructed in 1934 by the CCC') while its own structured 'Built' field says 1935. We reported both and treated the difference as likely reflecting start vs. completion/commission year rather than a factual error.

NHLR lists the tower as 11 feet; Recreation.gov separately describes the cabin as rising 10 feet above ground. These are close enough to likely be rounding of the same structure, not a true conflict, so we used the NHLR figure as primary.

notes_for_editor: No staffing history (first/last staffed, notable fires) found in the sources checked; story says so plainly rather than guessing. Minor built-year (1934 vs 1935) and tower-height (10' vs 11') discrepancies between NHLR's narrative and structured fields/Recreation.gov are noted but not fully resolved.
